title: Matt LaFleur wants team to 'stay focused on the task at hand' coming out of shortened bye
headline: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play Wednesday night at the Rams, Sean Rhyan is back at practice in a limited role, and Skyy Moore and Kevin Zeitler must prove themselves through the week.
summary: LaFleur said the shortened bye was awkward: he gave the staff one day off and the players a couple, with more time off coming later. He thinks the extra time could help, and said it let the staff watch tape for self-scouting instead of just looking at numbers. On injuries, Micah is expected to be on the practice field, and his practice performance will decide whether he plays. LaFleur is not anticipating Josh Jacobs for Wednesday and said he would have to prove he can function. Sean Rhyan is back at practice in a limited role, and LaFleur called him the starter who could help the line. Skyy Moore and Kevin Zeitler are among a group who must prove themselves this week, and LaFleur said the extra days help them. He praised Kaleb Johnson's growth and said learning protections was the hard part after a stretch of fumbles and inactive games. LaFleur called the Rams defense very sound with few weaknesses, and said their offense, with Stafford and a deep tight end group, is still dangerous without Puka and Davante. He stressed focusing on the process and the task at hand rather than the big picture.

LaFleur called it very sound and well coordinated under Chris Shula (whom he calls 'Schuler'). It has strong front-line players, plays man and soft zone well, and has few weaknesses.

He called Sean McVay as good as anyone, and said the team runs the ball well and has Matthew Stafford at quarterback. He said their tight end group is as complete as you can find, even without Puka and Davante.
The team added more competitive offense-versus-defense periods, giving a better read on the line and the Wednesday group.
LaFleur wants the team to stay focused on the day-to-day process and not look past a road prime-time game, noting seven games remain and the Rams were a preseason Super Bowl pick.

title: Sean McVay & Matthew Stafford on the Rams' bye week, valuing adaptability, facing the Packers & more
headline: Puka Nacua is out for some time after surgery, so Mumpfield, Daniels and Xavier Smith get WR work, while Kyren Williams (toe) and Blake Corum share the field in two-back sets.
summary: McVay opened with Wednesday's injury report. Four players did not practice (Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton and Terrance Ferguson with hamstrings, Kamren Curl with a toe). Kyren Williams and Myles Garrett were limited, and McVay said Kobie Turner is expected to practice. He said the Rams' offense has to stay flexible this season because of the skill-position players they are missing, and last week's Cardinals game showed that. The Rams used a lot of 13 personnel and two-back sets with Blake Corum and Kyren Williams together, and they threw on every snap from 20 personnel, though he joked they may run it more this week. He praised the young receivers who got chances and said the staff will lean into what each does best. He also said an interior lineman filled in well while the line shuffled, but the player is not clear from the captions. The Rams face the Packers on a Wednesday-night game after a bye, a compressed turnaround where they cannot ease back in. Stafford, speaking separately, said the Rams will miss Puka Nacua for some time after surgery. He also said the team's next-man-up approach and getting many players involved is what makes the offense hard to defend.

topics.detail: Wednesday-night game against the Packers after a bye, so the Rams have no bonus Monday to work back in. McVay said it feels closest to a Thursday game, with the focus needed right away.

McVay said the offense needs flexibility given the missing skill players. Last week featured plenty of 13 personnel and two-back sets, and the 20 personnel snaps were all passes. He said they might run it more this week, and that week-to-week adjustments continue.

McVay praised an interior lineman, not identifiable from the captions, for handling fronts and pressures while the line shuffled. He credited learning from Coleman Shelton. Avila, Shelton and Ferguson are all down with hamstrings, so the line is thin.

Stafford said the season has been next man up, with many moving parts on offense, defense and special teams. He said the offense is hard to defend when many players catch passes, including running backs like Ronnie Rivers.

title: Exclusive: Kellen Moore previews Week 11 at Bears
headline: Moore offered no new injury or role news; Tyson and Olave both stay involved in a deep receiver room, and the offensive line will be reshuffled again against Chicago's pass rush.
summary: Moore previewed the Week 11 game at Chicago, calling it a potentially explosive game in which turnover margin will be the key indicator. He said the Saints must protect the football, create and limit explosive plays, and treat the matchup as a fun one against a Bears team playing good football. Reflecting on the two recent home games (a split), he said the margins are tight, with turnovers and end-of-game situational football deciding games that came down to the final play. On the offensive line, which has been reshuffled because of injuries, he said the group will spend a full week together and be prepared, and that communication between the line, quarterback and backs on protection is crucial against a team that pressures the quarterback well. Asked how he manages the workload of Jordyn Tyson and Chris Olave, he praised both and the receiver room, mentioning another receiver, apparently Bailey, and said opportunities will present themselves rather than committing to a set split. On defense, he called Caleb Williams a really good quarterback who can make explosive plays from the pocket and be just as dangerous outside it, so controlling him is the key. No specific injury updates were given.
